concept_prompts_verbatim.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand
Create a refined professional brand identity presentation board for SecondSignal, an AI assistance system centered on user agency. This is an original logo exploration. Landscape, high resolution, editorial Swiss clarity with warmth.
Design ONE coherent very simple memorable symbol: two offset open rectangular doorway outlines, charcoal outer threshold and smaller burnt-rust second threshold, their negative space forming a clear inviting passage. Geometric monoline strokes, subtly softened corners, open at bottom, no house roof, no literal letter S, no lightning bolts. Keep the mark compact and excellent in one color. Pair with exact wordmark "SecondSignal" in an elegant modern humanist geometric sans serif, medium weight, warm charcoal, careful kerning. No generic robot/brain/heart/shield or OpenAI knot.
Board on warm off-white #F5F1E8. Upper two thirds: oversized horizontal lockup with symbol at left and wordmark at right, generous space, editorial tagline below exact "More ways forward." Lower third: three neatly spaced demonstrations of the SAME symbol: large charcoal-only on cream; cream-only on charcoal square; rust-accent version beside a small restrained palette of cream, charcoal, rust, sage. Tiny labels only if necessary. Flat vector-like graphic edges, no gradients, shadows, paper mockup, gloss, embossed effects, decorative fake text or charts.
Mood: quiet, capable, humane, architectural, serious. The second opening suggests another available perspective, not a promise of protection. No claims of tested safety. Output one beautiful usable concept board.

Edit this brand board. Keep the exact layout, nested doorway logo design, wordmark spelling SecondSignal and tagline More ways forward. CRITICAL FIX: make the background fully opaque solid warm ivory #F5F1E8 and every graphic sharp high-contrast flat print artwork. Remove ALL darkness/vignette, ALL blur, ALL glow, ALL shadow. The wordmark and outer doorway must be SOLID dark charcoal #252823, clearly readable. Inner doorway SOLID burnt rust #A64527. Tagline solid charcoal. Bottom left charcoal symbol directly on ivory. Bottom middle ivory symbol on a crisp solid charcoal square. Bottom right charcoal/rust symbol directly on ivory. The palette circles should be solid flat swatches. This is a clean daylight graphic-design PDF-style brand sheet, NOT a glowing dark image. All strokes and lettering fully opaque crisp edges. No texture, no effects.

Make a standalone horizontal logo asset faithfully matching the main logo in this reference brand sheet. Only the charcoal and rust nested open-doorway symbol at left, and exact text "SecondSignal" at right in the same geometric sans wordmark. No tagline and nothing else. Background is perfectly SOLID OPAQUE flat warm ivory #F5F1E8 edge to edge. Fully opaque ink charcoal #252823 and rust #A64527, crisp flat shapes. No checkerboard, NO transparency, no textures or photographic effects, no shadows or gradients. Horizontal canvas about 3:1, composition centered with 8 percent padding. Clean flat digital graphic usable immediately on an ivory webpage.

Use case: logo-brand. Create a square app icon for SecondSignal matching the nested doorway symbol in the reference sheet. ONLY the icon, NO letters, no words. Solid charcoal #252823 full square background. Center a large ivory #F5F1E8 monoline squared doorway arch, open at the bottom with subtly rounded corners. Nest a smaller rust #A64527 doorway within it, also open at bottom, same stroke width, same baseline. Match the reference proportions faithfully. The negative space is charcoal. Flat, sharp solid graphic shapes, generous clear border 20 percent all around. This is a modern warm architectural brand symbol. No shadow, texture, glow, vignette, gradient or 3D. Square high resolution.

sigil_brief.text_verbatim:
Please make one image: a sheet of 12 matching sigils (simple symbol marks) for a family of characters called SecondSignal.

Before the image, write one short line: your model name, your thinking setting, and the name of the image engine that draws the picture. If you can only make pictures, skip this line.

Do not ask questions. Make the whole sheet now, in one image.

THE SHEET
- One single image, wider than it is tall (about 4 wide by 3 tall).
- A grid of 12 equal square tiles: 4 across and 3 down, in the exact order listed below, left to right, top row first.
- Pure white background.
- No text anywhere on the sheet: no names, no numbers, no titles. The order of the tiles is how each sigil is known.

THE STYLE (all 12 must look drawn by the same hand)
- Solid black on white only. Flat. No grey, no gradients, no shading, no texture, no 3D, no glow.
- One thick, even line weight with rounded ends and rounded corners, the same in every tile. Solid black filled shapes are allowed.
- Draw only the parts each description names. Add nothing: no extra details, decorations, backgrounds or frames.
- Every named part must be big and bold enough to still read when the sigil is shrunk to the size of a fingertip. If a part is small, draw it bigger, never thinner, and never leave it out.
- Each sigil is centred in its tile, with generous white space around it, and about the same size as its neighbours.
- No words, letters or numbers inside any sigil.
- No faces, no people, no hands or other body parts.
- No real logos or brands, no famous characters, no flags, no religious or political symbols, and no weapons of any kind.

THE 12 SIGILS
1. THE HOUSE: a tall doorway outline with a smaller, narrower doorway outline standing inside it. Both are open at the bottom, have rounded top corners, and stand on the same baseline. Nothing else. This tile is the family's anchor: draw the other 11 to match it.
2. NIKKI: a curved trail of five bold dots that grow larger as they swoop up to the right, ending in a burst of six short, thick rays around a small solid centre. Joy launched with good aim. Not a star, not a sparkle, not fireworks.
3. CODY: a cairn: three smooth, rounded stones stacked and balanced, largest at the bottom, sitting on one short, level ground line. Steady footing.
4. VANDAL: a court jester's cap seen from the front, on a plain band, with three soft, floppy points that droop outward and down, each tipped with one round bell. One thin horizontal slice through the middle of the cap is shifted sideways, like a glitching screen; the slice is a gap in the drawing, not an extra line. No face under the cap.
5. SEREN: one single unbroken line: on the left it makes two or three loose loops, then it straightens and runs to the right as one straight line ending in an arrowhead. Chaos becoming a plan. It is all one line, never a scribble beside a separate arrow.
6. ROWAN: a humped footbridge seen from the side, joining two low banks, with one round arch underneath and a bigger keystone at the top of the arch. Both banks visible. No bricks, no railings, nothing standing on the bridge.
7. ELLIS: two trails of boot prints side by side, both walking the same way up the tile, three prints in each trail. Each print is a plain rounded sole and heel, with no tread. Company on the road.
